units.title: Counting Numbers: 1-10

outcomes.text: Count by 1s (forwards and backwards) to 10
Represent the number of objects in a group with a written numeral 0 to 10.
Count to answer “how many” questions (up to 5); Given a number to 5, count out how many objects
Identify, compare and order groups of 1 to 5 objects
Demonstrate an understanding of the relative size of numbers1 to 5, quickly naming a number that is 1 more or less than a number to 5, and solve related word problems (orally)
Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction by quickly naming a number that is 1 more or less than a number to 5
Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns by duplicating and extending element sound or action pattern

resources: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

units.title: Counting How Many: 1-10

outcomes.text: Count on or backwards from any number between 1 and 10
Count to answer “how many” questions (up to 10); Given a number to 10, count out how many objects
Partition or decompose 5 objects into 2 parts to identify combinations to 5 and record the partition symbolically
Identify, compare and order groups of 1 to 10 objects
Demonstrate addition/subtracting by acting out an ‘+’ or ‘–‘ word problem sums to 5, using putting together and counting all or taking away part and counting the rest.
Duplicate and extend 3 element sound or action pattern

resources: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

mental.title: Play “How Many Fingers Up” (using one hand)

mental.title: Play “Show me ___” numbers 1 to 5 with fingers

objectives: count out counters that match the number of fingers displayed in the air
match numerals cards with numbers shown by objects (or card)

activities.title_nl: O hum na lim a ƭak ake moƴu o may?

steps.text: Give pupils two numbers – e.g., 4 & 2. Have them work with a partner to take counters that represent each of the two numbers; and then identify which group of counters is more and justify their answer.
Han lay a lim a ƭak; Mbi’ yo ƭik ƭik njang limir na lim nuu refna; koy nu lalit a limum hupu, fu kum taxu.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.1.6.

activities.title: Play “Make a group with more/less than this number”

steps.text: Have each pupils make a group of counters (1 – 5). Call out a number and have them compare to see whether their groups are more/less than the number called out.
Make sure each pupil has counters up to 5 on their tables. Ask each pupil to make any group of counters (1 – 5).
Mbi’yo a keen, wiin ɗik nu mbokatir a limir

lessons.title: 1 Finding objects in groups of 2, 3, 4, …, 10 in the classroom

objectives: recognize objects in groups of 2, 3, 4, …, 10 in and around the classroom

steps.text: Have pupils count out loud each group of objects (from 5 to 9) found in the L1 Seereer and then in English.
Call out a number (5 to 9).

Repeat the activity with objects in pictures on the wall.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.1

closure.assessment: Take pupils to G1PB Activities 1.1.2 and point to the dot numbers for numbers you call, e.g., 5, 3, 7, etc.

lessons.title: Finding objects in groups of 2, 3, 4, …, 10 in the classroom

objectives: count to find in Seereer “how many” in a group of objects in and around the classroom

activities.title: Play “How many?”
activities.title_nl: O ŋas “podu num?”

steps.text: Put items up to 10 (pencils, books, pens, cards, sticks, etc. on a table, tins/boxes in the corner shop) and identify things not more than 10 in the classroom which all pupils can see, e.g., girls in a row, boys in a row, windows, books on the table, legs of the teacher’s table.
Han I lim pur I and a safe cangir (buk) “podu num” ndefu na taabulee”; Limandoor yo fa mi, leng, ƭik, tadik,
A safe cangir (buk) ƥetaafoleng ndef meek.
Write the numeral on the board, and ask the pupils to write it in their jotters
Mbind yo a limee me nu mbintaa.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.1.

closure.assessment: Take pupils to G1PB Activities 1.1.2. Point to a dot pattern and ask learners to point to the pattern in their books and say the number dots representing the number you call, e.g., 5, 3, 7, etc.

lessons.title: Before-before/After-after game
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: state the number that comes before and after a number called.

activities.title: “Before-before/After-after”
activities.title_nl: Mbi yo o ŋas balaa –balaa(adoox) / kaltaa – kaltaa

steps.text: We play the game standing and you respond Before when I say Before-before. When I call out a number you identify the number that comes before that number and say it. Anyone who calls the wrong number is out of the game and must sit down. Allow pupils to look at number line to find answer.
balaa –balaa /balaa:
• 3 → ƭik;
• 6 → ƥetik;
• 8 → ƥetaaƭaq; etc.
Repeat the came for After-after. When I call out a number you identify the number that comes after that number and say it. Anyone who calls the wrong number is out of the game and must sit down.
kaltaa - kaltaa / kaltaa:
• 3 → nahik;
• 6 → ƥetaaƭaq;
• 8 → ƥetaanahak; etc.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.3.

closure.assessment: Write the numbers 1 to 9 in any order on the board (i.e., 3, 5 8, 2, 6, etc.). Have learners come in turns to lead the “before-before/after-after game”, calling out the numbers on the board.
closure.homework: Ask learners play the “before-before/ after-after game” with their parent or sibling at home.

lessons.title: Ordering numerals 5 to 9
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: stand in the “order” of the numbers 5 to 9.

activities.title: Play “Stand in Order” Numbers between 5 and 10
activities.title_nl: O ŋas “ngeenoox yo ndeefir” a lim ndeer 5 fa 10

steps.text: Put 3 numbers on the board in random order. Say work with a partner to arrange the numbers from smallest to largest and justify the solution to the class. Place numeral cards between 5 and 10 turned upside down on a table.

Han I mbi’ o ŋas” ngeenoox yo ndeefir”. Han lay jaajang daduk de inoor na keen nuu refna de njil a karta a lim; De ƭeet a lim den ake a ngeenoox ne de ngupatirit na yo, ohe moƴna o neew (njanoon) mbaa no he moƴna may (ñamaak) koy a lalit too a kayit den. [Group with correct order or arrangement wins a point]
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.2 and 1.2.3

closure.assessment: Display numeral card (5 to 9) facing down. Ask learners to go in turns in groups of 4 to pick any four of the cards and arrange themselves in positions from smallest (left) to largest (right).

lessons.title: Compare two numbers using the More/less than Relation
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: stand in the “order” of the numbers 5 to 9.

activities.title: More or less than comparison story problems
activities.title_nl: A nax mbodatir, Moƴo may mbaa moƴo neew

steps.text: Give pupils situations shown below.
Awa a jega xa mangaru 8 Buba jeg 6 Har nu mbaagu o lay nu kaaga?
Encourage pupils to describe the situation by comparing. Examples of expected responses are:
Awa Moƴu mayiɗ,
Buba neewiɗitu tu xa ƭaq,
Awa Moƴu mayiɗ a Buba o ndik,
Buba Moƴu neew ɗit xa mangaru xa ƭaq, etc.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.4 and 1.2.5.

closure.assessment: Display numeral card (5 to 9) facing down. Ask learners to go in turns in pairs to pick a card each and show it to the class. Ask each to make a statement using the more/less than to compare the two numbers.
closure.homework: Ask learners to count the number of people in their family (or household) who are male and female. Then ask them to make a statement using the more/less than to compare the number of males and females.

lessons.title: Finding the rules for Sorting Objects into Groups
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Find different ways of comparing object based on size, color, shape, etc
Compare and order groups of up to 10 objects

activities.title: Finding the rules for sorting objects into groups
activities.title_nl: A baaƭ a ƭat pur xaajrand tikoorik na qaaj

steps.text: Present pupils with a collection of 3D objects of different types and colours; also, collections from the classroom corner shop.
Njil yo tikoorik ke na xa pokat. Har taxu nu mbokat tikoorik keek na xa pokat? Lim yo tikoorik ke ndef na no fokat nuu refna, nu mbindin me nu mbintaa mbaa no tabla le.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activity 1.3.1

closure.assessment: Give learners objects of different color and ask the learner to sort the objects based on color.

Compare and order groups of up to 10 objects

activities.title: Creating the rules for sorting 2D cutout shapes into groups

Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.3.2

closure.assessment: Give learners objects of different color and size, ask the learner to sort the objects into different groups and state how the sorting is done.
closure.homework: Ask pupils to find objects at home that look like shapes (e.g., plate, book, box, lid). They should sort them into groups: • Round shapes • 3-sided shapes • 4-sided shapes

lessons.title: Partitioning (Numbers 5, 6 and 7) into 2
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Partition numbers (5, 6 and 7) into 2 groups
Count the numbers in each group
materials: counters (e.g., sticks, seeds, beads or bottle caps)

activities.title: Partitioning (Numbers 5, 6 and 7) into 2
activities.title_nl: A qaaj a lim (5, 6 fu 7) 2

steps.text: Give pupils a number (5, 6 or 7), for example 6; have them count that number of counters and find the different ways of partitioning them into 2 groups. E.g., 5, is a group of 2 counters and a group of 3 counters”, i.e., 5 is (2, 3). Ask if they can find another different way of partitioning it?
Han I ƭeetoo a ƭat a lakas, naa I ngaajit kaa a lim na xa ƭak. Ƭeet yo a ƭat a lakas. Njang yo limir 6 nu ngaajin a keen a ƭak, nu layoo podum ref nu qaaj nuu ref na.
Have pupils take the 6 counters and find another way of partitioning it into two groups?
Ƭeet yo a ƭat, a lakas, ne 6 a waageena haajit ƭik. Ƭeet yo a ƭat, a lakas.
Repeat activity with another number, say 7 and 8.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.4.1 to 1.4.3

closure.assessment: Find another way of partitioning 7 counters into 2 groups
closure.homework: Have learners to partition 8 counters into 2 groups. Find the other ways?

lessons.title: Play “What can you tell me about…?” numbers 6 to 9

objectives: Describe numbers (6 to 9) by relating them to the size of other numbers on the number line

activities.title: Play “What can you tell me about…?” numbers 6 to 9
activities.title_nl: “Har nu mbaagaxam o lay nu…?” fa lim 6 bo 9.

steps.text: Describe a number by relating it to the sizes of other numbers using the number line. Encourage pupils to describe relative size of number by looking at the number line.
Han, I lay tig a lim, I mbodatirin fa lim a lakas mbi’tin o yuuƥ a lim... E.g., mbindax 7 hana ref:
- 7 refu ndeer 6 fa 8;
- 7 moƴu may 5 ndaa ten moƴu neew 10;
- 7 huptu 6, 1;
- 7 huptu 5, 2 etc.
Encourage pupils to describe relative size of number by looking at the number line.

closure.homework: Ask learners to describe 10 by relating it to the size of other numbers on the number line

lessons.title: How many altogether - sums less than 10

objectives: Put pairs of numbers whose sum is less than 10

Lalit yo a lim a ƭak a ƭak ake mbokatireena yo too ndefeer 6. Lalit yo har taxun.

closure.homework: sum (5) and justify/explain why, E.g., Which pairs do not make 5? (1, 4), (3, 3), (3, 2), (4, 2)

lessons.title: Two-element Picture Repeating Patterns

objectives: duplicate and extend 2 element picture patterns

Lalit yo nataal ne naa reef kaa. layo laam kum/ har Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activity 1.4.4

lessons.title: ‘How Many Altogether?’ story problems

objectives: Use counters to solve addition problems where total or sum is unknown

‘“Awa jega limir 5. Buba a ɓaatanin 3. Podu num a jega tu”? “Awa jega xa paƭ xa tadoom xa 4 koy Buba a jeg xa paƭ xa tadoom xa 3. Tica fee a ɓaatan o huu refna xa 4. xa paƭ xa tadoom xa podu num Buba a jegat tu?

Njal yo ƭik ƭik. Njal yo fu limir koy nu lalit nam nu mbi’ tun. Encourage them to build each group of counters and then put the two groups together to count the total number of counters (i.e., counting all strategy).
Nam nu mbi’ tun, pehe num nu mbintu ndax pehe a lim fopoo ndax a lim rek.

objectives: Read and write the number Zero (0)
Know the mean of Zero (0)

activities.title: The Concept of Zero
activities.title_nl: Ke ref na tus

steps.text: Have a set of books/counters on a table where all pupils can see. Start giving the books/counters away, one by one to pupils. Each time you give one away, have pupils identify how many you have left. Continue until you have given away all the books/counters, then ask a question.
Layaamo a karta a podu num mbaa a limir a podu num yoqɗeem ndiiki.
After pupils have proposed their ways of writing it, introduce the symbol “0”.
0 refu, tus mbaa dara refee maaga.

closure.homework: Ask the learners to write the number zero ten times on their jotters.

objectives: Identify the zero in real life situations
Understand the concept of zero

wiin fonum nu kalaas ne njegu a caf 5?
Xa tiiƭ xa podu num ndefu kam ngeeji ne?
A ƥanaana podu num ndefu na pañe le? (or other impossible situations).
Lay yo lakas no ñoow in kaa waageena lay tus.

objectives: Use counters to solve story problems involving subtraction to 10

lessons.title: What can you tell me about … (a given number)?

materials: Use counters as bottle tops or any other type of counters.
